about: The attention items on the mock floor `AGENT_IDE_MOCK=attention` (the junior floor plus seven sessions with one of each kind, and a Claude Code session stopped on AskUserQuestion with a background subagent; see workspace/fixtures/junior-swe/FIXTURE.md), a freshly started server each run, since answering in the list uses up the mock's three open requests (they are resolved by the mock itself, never sent to an agent) and the mock's next events (`mock` steps: the person answering in Claude Code, the subagent reporting back, a second turn) happen once. Run at 1440x900 with ?tick=1&minimap=inline (the mini-map steps are skipped without it). One telling (map engine, plan D18): every surface reads the engine's one list, one entry per agent that needs you (it asks, its last turn failed, it finished and you have not looked, or it is silent); no icon stands over a column and no line above it: the agent's mark takes its logo's place (its floor label or the top of its stack), and the logo of every listed agent is hidden. The words (asks you, failed, finished, silent) are on its row in the list and on its edge mark's hover. A Claude Code session stopped on AskUserQuestion is a question waiting on you (its column, its mini-map row, the tree's head), answered in Claude Code, never from here, and gone once the transcript has the answer. A subagent's hand-back is no item: never in the tree's head count or the list, only a short pulse from the child to its parent, gone a few seconds later. The error mark (2026-11-09) means the agent's latest turn failed and you have not looked: a failure followed by work is none (the receipts agent's two, a resumed subagent's), a subagent's failure folded into its parent's row stands on the parent's column and a click on that column clears it (where the engine lists such a subagent on its own the mini-map steps use it; otherwise they are skipped). A click on the agent itself (its column or stub, its mini-map row, its edge mark, its row in the list) clears what only tells you something, once: a finished answer, an error, a quiet clock; the entry goes from the list, the edge, the tray's count and the mini-map's 'N for you', the column's logo comes back, and a reload does not bring it back; a question or an approval stays until answered. A click on its row in the list: back to now (the rail rewound first), the camera on the column, its chat open (an error's chat shows the failed turn in its own row). Edges: after a flight, the columns off screen show at the view's edge, and the one behind the chat window at the window's edge; hover words it, a click goes there. The tray: first in the top-right row, its badge the number of agents on the list (not requests), orange while any asks; its list one ordered list, the agents that ask first (by urgency, then the longest wait), the same count; a question and an approval answered in the list; a row click closes it and opens that chat; mark all read leaves only the agents that ask. The steps take the agents by name through the list's hit names (tray-row:<agent>:<condition>, condition asking, failed, finished or stalled); the old hover steps on icons over columns are gone with the icons. The finished mark (2026-11-09) means the agent has returned and you have not looked: an unread answer keeps its agent from going inactive (2026-11-10; plans/inactive.json), gone while it works again (the Claude app's registration busy, or a new message in its transcript) and back when that turn ends, one per column; a turn begun with the registration idle keeps the agent running in the mini-map (no flip to finished). A Claude Code session the Claude app holds shows a line above its chat's box and a 'send as copy' button; the send asks first; a copy is a column of its own named 'copy of …'. The page is loaded again between flights (the read marks live in the browser's local storage, so they stay).
